one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-09 to 2026-11-08. The stock just fell 13.3% in one day (worst since 2011 per NBC) on SpaceX's deal to buy Grain's nationwide 800 MHz spectrum (up to 14 MHz paired), which still needs FCC approval [1][2][4]. Scheduled in window: T-Mobile Q3 2026 results and call on 2026-10-28 (release ~4:05pm ET) [21]; Verizon/AT&T Q3 prints are also expected in late October (dates not confirmed by me, judgment). What I expect from Q3: the 2026 plan migration of ~4M legacy customers (TD Cowen sees ~$288M annual revenue uplift) is a churn risk for the quarter [12]; account churn was already up 7bp YoY to 0.99% in Q2 [15], and the company no longer discloses postpaid phone net adds, so the market will read account adds/ARPA and any comment on SpaceX [9]. Guidance (EBITDA $37.1-37.5B, adj FCF $18.4-18.8B) was raised in July [14] and is unlikely to be cut on Q3 alone; a reiteration plus buyback cadence at depressed prices is mildly supportive, while any 2027 commentary on promotions is the downside risk. Short-horizon regularities pull both ways: partial reversal after an event-driven gap on a long-dated threat vs. continued negative momentum (-34% over 12 months, at 52-week low). Net: no directional edge, so a near-symmetric distribution centred at ~$149 with ~10% monthly vol (33%/3.5 = 9.4%, nudged up for the earnings event and post-shock regime), with slightly fat tails.

bear.story: FCC approves SpaceX-Grain 800 MHz deal and Starlink Mobile pricing plus cable MVNO share gains force retention spend; Q3/Q4 show rising churn from the plan migration; 2027 EPS ~$13 and the stock rerates to Verizon-like ~8.5x (VZ 8.2x fwd today). Buyback authorization expires 2026-12-31 and a smaller 2027 program disappoints.

base.story: Guidance delivered, FCF ~$19-20B in 2027 retires ~5% of shares a year; SpaceX remains a narrative overhang (analysts see years to scale, carriers refuse MVNO) but not a P&L event by Oct-2027; multiple settles ~10.5x NTM EPS, a small premium to peers.

bull.story: Threat fades (FCC delay, SpaceX strategy shifts, no MVNO), Q3/Q4 beat with strong account adds, new large 2027 shareholder-return program bought at depressed prices; rerating toward 13.5x NTM EPS (~$15.2), still below sell-side average target $241.5.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: A small premium only: TMUS's 3y EPS growth forecast is 17.0% vs a peer median of 7.6% and its FCF is still growing (Q2 +4%), with leverage at 2.3x. But the growth premium is eroding: account adds fell 13% YoY in Q2 and ARPA grew only ~2%, management stopped disclosing postpaid phone net adds (critics: 'they retire it when they fear the optics'), cable MVNOs took 5.6% of switchers in Q1 vs 4.2% a year earlier, and SpaceX now has low-band spectrum. Much of EPS growth is buybacks. So I give back most of the historic premium rather than assume it persists. CHTR's 2.3x fwd P/E is an outlier and does not drive the median materially. DTEGY consolidates TMUS so it is partly circular.

thesis_break_reason: $115 is ~7.5x the $15.25 FY28 EPS estimate and ~15% FCF yield on the 2026 FCF guide ($18.6B on a ~$123B market cap). A sustained trade there would mean the market prices falling FCF: e.g. a guidance cut at Q3/Q4, an industry price war after FCC approval of the SpaceX spectrum deal, or a sharply smaller 2027 buyback. That is the bear case happening, not ordinary volatility (-23% from here).

key_uncertainties: How fast and how credibly SpaceX can turn EchoStar 2 GHz plus Grain 800 MHz spectrum into a competitive mobile service (analysts: years; Moffett: 'extraordinarily challenging' within five years without an MVNO).
Whether competitive pressure shows up as price/ARPA erosion and retention spend before any subscriber loss (Scotiabank and Bernstein flag valuation pressure and share-taking dynamics).
Reduced disclosure: no postpaid phone net adds since Q1 2026 makes deterioration harder to detect early.
Size of the 2027 buyback program after the current authorization expires 2026-12-31; buybacks drive a large part of EPS growth.
Controlled-company governance: DT holds 53.7% of votes; a revived holdco deal may not pay minorities a premium; SoftBank has a VPF on 10M shares.
Management turnover in 2026: new CEO (Q1 2026 first full quarter), CBPO departure, CFO transition in Feb 2027.
Price-lock class action and mass arbitration (Oddo v. T-Mobile) and FCC complaints: reputational more than financial so far.
reasoning: Starting point: $148.58 after a -13.3% day on 2026-10-09 (prev close $171.31) [1], 34% below a year ago. The catalyst is SpaceX agreeing to buy Grain's nationwide 800 MHz portfolio (the spectrum T-Mobile divested after Sprint), giving Starlink Mobile building-penetrating low band on top of EchoStar 2 GHz; FCC approval pending; carriers lost >$50B of value in a morning [2][3]. Bear evidence I weighed: (a) the threat has steadily compressed sector multiples all year (Bernstein July PT $245->$220, Scotiabank $232->$217->$212, valuation pressure from SpaceX) [4][5][6]; (b) operating growth is slowing: Q2 postpaid account adds 277k (-13% YoY), account churn 0.99% (+7bp), ARPA +2% [14][15]; (c) T-Mobile stopped disclosing postpaid phone net adds, prepaid and fiber adds in Q1 2026, which Recon's Entner reads as fear of optics, and cable MVNOs' switcher share rose to 5.6% [9]; (d) churn risk from migrating ~4M legacy-plan customers amid price-lock litigation [12]; (e) management churn (CBPO out July, CFO retiring Feb 2027) [17][18]; (f) controlled-company/overhang issues: DT 53.7% control, SoftBank VPF on 10M shares, stalled DT holdco plan where New Street saw limited premium for minorities [10][11][19]. What I checked and did not find: material insider selling (latest Form 144 is 772 shares) [20], short-seller reports, accounting restatements, or leverage stress (net debt/EBITDA 2.3x) [15]. Weighing honestly: the counter-evidence is strong; analysts quoted by Reuters/NBC and T-Mobile's own executives argue SpaceX needs years and a terrestrial network, carriers refuse an MVNO [2][7][8], and TMUS still guides $18.4-18.8B adj FCF (~11.7% of market cap) with an $18.2B return program [14]. Valuation: three methods anchored on a 10-peer set (median fwd P/E 9.9x, EV/EBITDA 6.9x) with only a small premium kept for TMUS's growth give ~$154 at the horizon. Scenarios: bear $112 (25%), base $157 (55%), bull $205 (20%); expected ~$157, median ~$155. I built the ladder as a mixture of lognormals around those scenarios (log sd 0.23/0.17/0.17), giving an overall dispersion ~28% log sd, a bit under the 33% realized vol because realized includes the one-off shock, with tails floored for gap risk. P(>= $149) = 0.56 reflects slight upside to fair value; P(>= $223) only 7.5% because I do not expect the pre-2026 premium multiple to return within a year. The sell-side average target ($241.5) is stale relative to the shock and has been cut repeatedly, so I treat it as an upper-bound sentiment marker, not an anchor. Lane note: 14 of 33 sources are lane-specific (sell-side cuts, critical journalism, filings on insiders/governance/management turnover, litigation); the 10 peer-statistics pages required by the comps rule are data sources, and excluding them 14 of 23 (61%) are in lane. Several pages (Forbes, CNBC, Benzinga, Fierce, IR site) blocked fetching; sec.gov archives refused scripted access so filings were read via WebFetch; Twelve Data fundamentals/estimates were paywalled. Credit ratings and bond spreads could not be confirmed at source and were left out.
